clue.text: Connect annexe for Spooner, getting out with difficulty

indicators.note: the clue asks for the two words as Spooner would say them, swapping their first sounds

parts.note: to connect is to link
an annexe is a wing added to a building

explanation.surface: An instruction to join an extension onto a building, struggling as you go.
explanation.walkthrough: LINK WING with its opening letters exchanged becomes WINK LING.
explanation.definitionFit: To winkle something out is to extract it slowly and awkwardly, like a periwinkle from its shell with a pin.

clue.text: Cocktail that sounds like it has a hold on me?

indicators.note: the clue says the drink's name is spoken the same as the phrase that follows

parts.words: it has a hold on me?
parts.note: a necktie grips the wearer's own neck, so it is my tie

explanation.surface: A drink so potent it seems to have a grip on the drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition-by-example of a necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: A mai tai is a rum-based tiki drink with lime and orgeat.

clue.text: Provision rejected in Edinburgh

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the hidden run of letters is read in reverse
in says the letters sit inside the name of the Scottish capital

explanation.surface: Supplies turned away in the Scottish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is slang for food, and provisions are stocks of food.

clue.text: Misled, lost head, and fled?

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: to be misled is to be deluded

explanation.surface: Someone deceived who panicked and ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the definition is loose: getting away from pursuers is a form of flight.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade or escape a pursuer is close in sense to running away from them.

clue.text: Country set?

definitions.meaning: the People's Republic in East Asia
porcelain, as in a set of fine tableware such as a tea service

explanation.surface: A query whether a nation is fixed or decided.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asian nation shares its name with porcelain crockery, often sold as a matching dinner or tea set.

clue.text: Add calorie on top of skimmed sweet drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top of puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for calorie

indicators.note: skimming takes off the top layer, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a toffee is a chewy sweet

explanation.surface: Diet advice: putting extra calories on top of a skimmed-milk sweet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skimmed' and 'drink' suggest a milky beverage, but 'skimmed' acts on the sweet, giving OFFEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee is a hot beverage brewed from roasted beans.

clue.text: Show clue for Tom's tricycle?

parts.note: the show's title works as an anagram clue: its first two words are the fodder and its last word the signal, and the shuffled letters spell this phrase

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter asking for a clue to a boy's three-wheeler.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer itself is a working cryptic clue whose solution is the phrase in the clue. Strictly Come Dancing is the BBC's celebrity ballroom contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a long-running British television entertainment programme of celebrity ballroom contests.

clue.text: Skiing regularly leads to envy, possibly

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the word, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Going down the slopes often makes others jealous.
explanation.walkthrough: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins, hence 'possibly' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins, so it is an example of a moral transgression.

clue.text: Suitable leaders of children's holiday activities go after Conservative — it proves humanity

indicators.note: the pieces before these words are placed after the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: suitable means apt

indicators.note: leaders are the opening letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Fitting summer activities for kids follow a Tory party policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces run C, then APT, then CHA from the initials of 'children's holiday activities'.
explanation.definitionFit: The website test of distorted letters or images checks that a visitor is a person rather than a bot.

clue.text: Note taken badly — it may suggest exposure

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A message written down carelessly might reveal secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottled bronze from a lotion gives the look of time spent in the sun without real sunbathing.

clue.text: Piebald surprisingly walking upright

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something turned out in an unexpected form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patchy black-and-white horse astonishingly up on two legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature going about on two legs, like a human, stands erect as it moves.

clue.text: When hot, follows Latin beat

indicators.note: follows puts the earlier pieces after the abbreviation named next

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A rhythm heats up after a Latin dance tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a musical noun but is the verb to whip.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash is to strike repeatedly with a whip, a synonym of beat as a verb.

clue.text: Extracts energy, legal up to a point

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
licit means lawful
S is a compass point, south

explanation.surface: Drawing out power in a way that is only partly lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to a point' reads as 'partly' but is just LICIT next to S.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out a response or information from someone is to elicit it, a synonym for extracting.

clue.text: References heard for positions

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as it is spoken, not as it is written

parts.note: cites are references, as in citations in a paper

explanation.surface: Citations listened to when job candidates apply for posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are locations or places where things stand, a synonym for positions.

clue.text: With internal publicity, confronts illusions

indicators.note: with internal says the publicity goes inside the word that follows

parts.note: to confront is to face
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A publicist promoting from within who confronts popular misconceptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A false front is a show put up to deceive, so the plural fits deceptive appearances.

clue.text: Sacked or let off

definitions.meaning: discharged, as a gun or firework

explanation.definitionFit: A dismissed employee is shown the door, and a discharged gun or rocket has been shot.

clue.text: Bet tall girl, 21, gets 6 24 21 prize

indicators.note: 21-across gives the word dancing, and letters that dance are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A wager that a tall girl will win the trophy of a TV ballroom show.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 21 is itself the anagram signal. The Glitterball trophy goes to the winners of Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The mirrored disco ball trophy is awarded to the winning couple of the BBC ballroom show.

clue.text: Here in France, caught the French descendants in cold weather?

parts.note: ici is French for here
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
les is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A French genealogical record of offspring found during a frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descendants' suggests family heirs; the question mark warns that it means things that hang down.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen spikes of water hang downwards from eaves in frosty spells, so they are literally things that descend.

clue.text: Gnarly old tree I hung around

indicators.note: gnarly means twisted and knotted, so these letters are contorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker idling under a knotted ancient tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or linger aimlessly in a place is to hang around.

clue.text: House-sitter keeps applications

indicators.note: keeps says the letters are held within the run of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone minding a home holds on to some requests.
explanation.definitionFit: Uses are the purposes something is put to, a synonym for its applications.

clue.text: Matures, holds on, and settles

indicators.note: holds says the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: something that matures ages
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Wine that grows older, carries on and finally settles.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to terms on a deal or a dispute is to settle it.

clue.text: View five siblings on the air, or thousands on 6 24 21

indicators.note: on the air means broadcast and so spoken aloud

parts.note: to view is to see; five siblings born together are quins

explanation.surface: Watching a family of quintuplets on TV, or a sparkly ballroom show.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE QUINS spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny shiny discs are sewn by the thousand onto the ballroom costumes on the BBC dance show.

clue.text: Suppresses queens, replacing English nationalist with liberals

indicators.note: replacing tells us one pair of letters is swapped out for another

parts.note: the word queens is taken as written
E is English and N nationalist
L is liberal, so two liberals are LL

explanation.surface: Monarchs swapping a patriot for progressives to crush dissent.
explanation.walkthrough: In QUEENS, EN is swapped for LL.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down a rebellion or calm a fear is to subdue it, a synonym of crushing.

clue.text: See 6
Recognise description of fake diamonds?

parts.note: something fake is not the real thing, so the word not
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: How a jeweller identifies a description of counterfeit gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'description of' frames the pair: fake diamonds are 'not ice'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot or become aware of something is to recognise it.

clue.text: Gloss given by oil company account

parts.note: Shell is a major oil company

explanation.surface: A shine supplied by a petroleum firm's report.
explanation.definitionFit: The resin varnish is a glossy finish applied to wood.

clue.text: See 6
Outlying motorway cuts through ruined Exeter

indicators.note: cuts through means one piece slices inside the other
ruined says the letters of the city are wrecked into another order

parts.note: M is a motorway, as in the M5

explanation.surface: A distant motorway slicing through a wrecked Devon city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns EXETER into EXTREE, and 'cuts through' puts M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at the very edge or farthest limit is remote or outermost.

clue.text: Retreat from eager beaver's bossiness at first

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Backing off from a keen worker's domineering manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide's going out is a withdrawal, and to recede is to retreat.

clue.text: Expose yourself to the mafia in brief public assembly

parts.note: to flash is to expose oneself indecently
the Mob is a name for the mafia

explanation.surface: An indecent display to gangsters in a short crowd gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd that gathers suddenly by arrangement, performs and disperses is a brief public gathering.

clue.text: Tasteful crop is back in hairdresser catalogues

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of the two words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tasteful haircut appears again in a salon's brochures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop' suggests a haircut alongside the hairdresser, but it is a plant grown to eat. I added 'in' to the draft as the signal for the concealed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The peppery salad seedling is a cultivated plant valued for its flavour.
